scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Users on PC1 (10.1.0.100) in Office A report they cannot reach
anything outside their own VLAN. Internal pings to other Office-A
data PCs still work, but Internet access and reaching Office B
services hang. Investigate.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r1 ospfd daemon
Mechanism: r1 stopped sending OSPF hellos and LSAs. CSW1/CSW2
  aged out r1's loopback (10.0.0.76) and the default route r1
  originated via `default-information originate`. Office-A
  internal traffic still works because DSWs route locally,
  but anything beyond the OSPF backbone (Internet, Office B
  via core) has no next hop and is dropped.
Localization: r1
Root cause: OSPF routing daemon (ospfd) not running on r1
Fix: restart frr on r1 — `/etc/init.d/frr restart`

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on r1" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: DNS service (BIND/named) on srv1 (10.5.0.4). Mechanism: PC1 uses 10.5.0.4 for DNS (resolv.conf). L3 routing is healthy (pc1 can ping 10.3.0.100 and 10.5.0.4), but name resolution breaks: for public domains the resolver refuses recursion, and for internal names everything under jeremysitlab.com resolves to srv1 due to a wildcard, so connections hit the wrong host and appear to “hang.”

Localization: On srv1, named is running and configured as authoritative-only. Evidence:
- From pc1: nslookup example.com 10.5.0.4 returns “REFUSED.”
- On srv1: /etc/bind/named.conf sets “recursion no;” and listen-on any; zone file /etc/bind/db.jeremysitlab contains a wildcard “* IN A 10.5.0.4,” mapping any campus hostname to srv1.
- Routing between VLANs is fine: pc1→pc3 (10.3.0.100) and pc1→srv1 (10.5.0.4) pings succeed, proving the issue is not L3.

Root cause: Misconfigured DNS on srv1 (authoritative-only with recursion disabled and a wildcard zone) causes external lookups to be refused and internal hostnames to resolve to the DNS server’s IP, making “Internet access” and Office B services appear unreachable.

Corrective fix: On srv1, enable recursion and provide forwarders to reachable recursive resolvers (or allow full recursion with root hints if upstream exists). Replace the wildcard with proper A/AAAA records (or delegate zones) for real internal hosts. Example: set “recursion yes;” and configure forwarders in named.conf.options; remove the wildcard and add correct records. Reload BIND (systemctl reload bind9 or rndc reload).

per_axis.rationale: The agent blamed srv1 (DNS) rather than identifying r1 as the affected device (ospfd), so it did not meet the requirement to identify r1.
The submission diagnoses DNS issues on srv1 and does not identify ospfd/OSPF routing as the affected component.

The diagnosis explains the mechanism: recursion disabled yields REFUSED for external lookups, and the wildcard A record causes internal names to resolve to srv1 so traffic goes to the wrong host (appearing to hang).
The agent recommends changing BIND configuration on srv1 (enable recursion, remove wildcard), which does not match the expected remediation of restarting FRR on r1.

The agent's DNS-focused claims are well-supported by observed outputs (nslookup, named.conf, process list), but their inference that DNS misconfiguration is the root cause of the reported reachability problem is a leap and they failed to check router/OSPF state (the true fault).
